Class Scanner

java.lang.Object
java.io.Reader
easyIO.BacktrackScanner
easyIO.Scanner
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable, Readable
public class Scanner extends BacktrackScanner
A BacktrackScanner extended with convenience methods for parsing common things like integers and identifiers. Compared to a java.util.Scanner, it has the ability to peek() at the next character on the input and the ability to read its input from multiple Readers, which may be added on the fly. Beyond this, it can also do arbitary lookahead and rollback of the input stream using the mark(), accept(), and abort() methods from BacktrackScanner. Generally, all methods parse input starting at the current position, and throw UnexpectedInput if the expected input is not found. If an exception is thrown, the current input position is left unchanged.

    • nextMatches

      public List<Match> nextMatches(Matcher m) throws UnexpectedInput
      Scan past the longest prefix of the input, starting at the current position, that matches the regular expression of m, and return all the ways it matches, with their captures. Capture positions are relative to the start of the matched text, which is group(0) of each match. The prefix may be empty if the regular expression matches the empty string; then the input position does not change, so a loop that calls this method until it fails will not terminate. Whitespace is not skipped. Finding the longest prefix may require reading ahead past it.
      Throws:
      UnexpectedInput - if no prefix matches. The input position is then left unchanged.

    • next

      public String next(Matcher m) throws UnexpectedInput
      Scan past and return the longest prefix of the input, starting at the current position, that matches the regular expression of m. Like nextMatches(m), but faster because captures are not computed.
      Throws:
      UnexpectedInput - if no prefix matches. The input position is then left unchanged.

    • next

      public String next(String pattern) throws UnexpectedInput
      Scan past and return the longest prefix of the input, starting at the current position, that matches the regular expression pattern, written in the syntax of easyIO.regexp.Parser. The pattern is parsed once and cached.
      Throws:
      UnexpectedInput - if no prefix matches. The input position is then left unchanged.
      IllegalArgumentException - if the pattern is not a valid regular expression.
